message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the most important rights and protections you have as a residential tenant in Texas. These rights come from the Texas Property Code (the state’s landlord‑tenant law), federal fair‑housing statutes, and, in some cases, local ordinances (e.g., Austin, Dallas, Houston). The information is meant to help you understand your position; it is **not** legal advice. If you have a specific dispute or need personalized guidance, consult a licensed attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization. --- ## 1. **Security Deposit & Move‑In/Move‑Out Procedures** | Issue | Texas Law (Property Code) | Key Points | |-------|---------------------------|------------| | **Maximum Deposit** | § 24.001 | For a single‑unit dwelling, the landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent**. For a multi‑unit building, up to **two months’ rent**. | | **Deposit Return** | § 24.002 | Must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, unless the landlord gives a written statement of deductions. | | **Deductions** | § 24.003 | Deductions may cover unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear, or cleaning costs if the unit is not left in a “clean and habitable” condition. | | **Written Notice** | § 24.004 | Landlord must provide a written itemized list of deductions within **30 days** of the move‑out date. | | **Interest** | § 24.005 | Landlords are **not required** to pay interest on security deposits. | > **Tip:** Keep a copy of the lease, move‑in inspection report, and any receipts for repairs or cleaning. These documents help you contest improper deductions. --- ## 2. **Habitability & Repairs** | Issue | Texas Law | Key Points | |-------|-----------|------------| | **Implied Warranty of Habitability** | § 24.006 | Landlord must keep the premises in a livable condition—plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control. | | **Repair Requests** | § 24.007 | Tenants must notify the landlord in writing (email, text, or letter) of needed repairs. | | **Landlord’s Obligation** | § 24.008 | Must make reasonable repairs within a **reasonable time**. | | **Tenant Remedies** | § 24.009 | If the landlord fails to repair, you may:
• Pay for the repair and deduct the cost from rent (with written notice).
• Withhold rent (after giving written notice).
• Terminate the lease (after giving written notice).
• File a lawsuit for damages. | > **Note:** Texas does not allow “repair‑and‑deduct” or “rent‑withholding” without first giving the landlord written notice and a reasonable opportunity to fix the problem. --- ## 3. **Rent & Lease Terms** | Issue | Texas Law | Key Points | |-------|-----------|------------| | **Rent Increases** | § 24.010 | Landlords may increase rent at the end of a lease term or with a **30‑day written notice** for month‑to‑month agreements. | | **Late Fees** | § 24.011 | Late fees are allowed but must be **reasonable** and disclosed in the lease. | | **Lease Termination** | § 24.012 | Either party may terminate a month‑to‑month lease with **30 days’ written notice**. | | **Security Deposit vs. Rent** | § 24.013 | Security deposit is **not** considered rent; it is refundable. | --- ## 4. **Privacy & Entry Rights** | Issue | Texas Law | Key Points | |-------|-----------|------------| | **Landlord Entry** | § 24.014 | Landlord may enter only for:
• Repairs or inspections.
• Showing the unit to prospective tenants or buyers.
• In emergencies. | | **Notice Requirement** | § 24.015 | Must give **at least 24 hours’ written notice** (unless emergency). | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | § 24.016 | Landlord must not disturb your peaceful use of the premises. | --- ## 5. **Fair Housing & Discrimination** | Issue | Federal Law | Texas Law | |-------|-------------|-----------| | **Protected Classes** | Fair Housing Act (FHA) | Texas Property Code § 24.017 (no discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or age). | | **Reasonable Accommodations** | FHA | Landlords must provide reasonable accommodations for disabilities (e.g., wheelchair ramps). | | **Retaliation** | FHA | Landlords cannot retaliate against tenants who file complaints or exercise rights. | > **Tip:** If you suspect discrimination, you can file a complaint with the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or the Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR). --- ## 6. **Eviction Process** | Step | Texas Law | Key Points | |------|-----------|------------| | **Notice to Pay or Quit** | § 24.018 | Landlord must give a **3‑day notice** (or 30 days for month‑to‑month) to pay overdue rent or vacate. | | **Notice to Cure or Quit** | § 24.019 | For lease violations, a **30‑day notice** to cure or quit. | | **Unlawful Detainer Action** | § 24.020 | If the tenant does not comply, the landlord files an unlawful detainer lawsuit. | | **Court Judgment** | § 24.021 | If the court rules in favor of the landlord, the tenant must vacate within **10 days** of the judgment. | | **Eviction Notice** | § 24.022 | Landlord must serve a **10‑day notice** to vacate after a judgment. | > **Important:** Texas courts do not allow “self‑help” evictions (e.g., changing locks). Doing so can expose the landlord to civil liability. --- ## 7. **Local Ordinances & Additional Protections** | City | Key Local Ordinance | What It Adds | |------|---------------------|--------------| | **Austin** | Austin Housing Code § 5.1 | Limits rent increases to **5%** per year for certain units; requires landlords to provide a “Move‑In/Move‑Out Checklist.” | | **Dallas** | Dallas Rent Control Ordinance | Caps rent increases for certain units; requires landlords to provide a “Tenant Handbook.” | | **Houston** | Houston Housing Code § 3.1 | Requires landlords to provide a “Tenant Rights & Responsibilities” pamphlet. | > **Check your city’s website** for the most recent ordinances, as they can change. --- ## 8. **Resources & Where to Get Help** | Resource | What It Offers | |----------|----------------| | **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** | Free legal information, consumer guides, and a lawyer referral service. | | **Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR)** | Handles discrimination complaints. | | **HUD – Fair Housing Hotline** | 1‑800‑669‑6767 (24/7). | | **Local Tenant‑Rights Organizations** | e.g., “Texas Tenants’ Rights” (non‑profit), “Austin Tenants’ Union.” | | **Legal Aid Societies** | e.g., “Legal Aid of North Texas,” “Houston Legal Aid.” | | **Online Lease Templates** | Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) provides sample lease agreements. | --- ## Quick Checklist for Tenants 1. **Read the lease** carefully before signing. 2. **Document the unit’s condition** with photos and a written inspection report. 3. **Keep copies** of all communications with the landlord (emails, texts, letters). 4. **Know your notice periods** for moving out or terminating a lease. 5. **Report repairs** in writing and keep a record of the landlord’s response. 6. **Understand your rights** to privacy, habitability, and fair housing. 7. **Seek help early** if you face eviction threats or discrimination. --- ### Bottom Line As a Texas tenant, you have the right to a safe, habitable home, a fair and transparent process for security deposits and rent, the right to privacy, and protection against discrimination. If a landlord violates these rights, you have several remedies—from repair‑and‑deduct to filing an unlawful detainer suit. When in doubt, reach out to a local tenant‑rights group or a qualified attorney to ensure your rights are fully protected.
